files.legend.sop:
@legend.core core.legend
    namespace=core
    version=0.1.0
    doc="Bootstrap legend: the types and keys every other legend builds on. Dynamic keys: a core.key with dynamic=true declares a key prefix; a wire may use any key of the form <prefix>.<anything> (for example where.owner or arg.count on core.question and core.request). The part after the prefix is resolved against the wire type named by the question, and the value kind is any."

@core.thing core.type
    doc="Root of the type hierarchy; any wire without an explicit parent extends it."

@core.state core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A fact that holds at some time: something has a property or relation."

@core.event core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="Something that happens; events are ordered by core.seq in dialog order."

@core.agent core.type
    extends=core.thing
    shared=true
    doc="A person or participant that can be mentioned in dialog."
    example="Tom"

@core.question core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A question about a wire type: type, seek, optional where.<key> constraints (see the legend doc), mode."

@core.answer core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="The result of resolving a question or request, written by the interpreter."

@core.request core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A request to run an action operation: action and optional arg.<name> arguments (see the legend doc)."

@core.legend core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A legend: namespace, version, imports."

@core.type core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A type declaration."

@core.key core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A key declaration."

@core.world core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A world manifest."

@core.pattern core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A rule-formalizer pattern."

@core.operation core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="An operation declaration."

@core.template core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="An answer rendering template."

@core.test core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A competency test."

@core.lexicon core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A word list."

@core.phrase core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A phrase macro: a named group of literal alternatives that patterns use as [$id] (spec 03 section 2.5)."

@core.shape core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A request shape: one operation (family, verbs, object, value, emit) from which the request forms are generated as patterns at load (spec 03 section 2b)."

@core.describe core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="An operation description: one operation (op, intent, emit, frames). Its arguments are core.describe.arg wires, its wording one core.describe.words wire per language, its words core.word wires; request, question and statement patterns are generated from them (spec 03 section 2c). Read only with PSYS_GEN_PATTERNS."

@core.describe.arg core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="One argument role of an operation description: of (the description), name, class (a lexicon id, number, rest, noun, words), size (the maximum of words), optional=true, qty (the count slot of a quantified item), slot (the slot of the legend the argument fills, spec 16 section 8)."

@core.describe.words core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="The wording of one operation description in one language: of (the description), lang, then repeated keys whose values are core.word wires: verb tverb noun ask rest pre mid subject, and for an argument prep.<name> det.<name> unit.<name>; nosubject=true; sample.<slot>=value; example (sentences)."

@core.word core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A word and the name it means (the library's core.word; words have no language, sopworld 0.13): text, means (an operation's emit key, an argument as <op>.<name>, or a value of a slot, with of naming the slot)."

@core.note core.type
    extends=core.thing
    doc="A free-text note (SOP Lang v1 has no comments)."

    value=atom

    ask="which wire types?"
    doc="Wire types that the world's matrix actions write and other worlds read from the session memory (for example kids.tasks.entry for charts and documents). With reasoner=matrix the host layer copies them from the library's World into the session memory after every action."

@core.world.source core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="how does the world call its own facts?"
    doc="The phrase \"why?\" uses for facts that no sentence of the dialogue told, after \"from\" (for example \"the price list\", \"what I know about animals\"). Without it the phrase is \"what I know\"."

@core.world.ops core.key
    value=atom
    card=many
    ask="which keys?"
    doc="With reasoner=matrix: keys (type.key, for example kids.shapes.thing.is_color) whose questions the matrix leaves to the operations of the world (ops.mjs): checks that carry the value they seek (\"is a banana red?\": a library query would answer the value it was given) and lookups that read the facts in both orders. A question about one of them is never asked to the library."

@core.world.compose core.key
    value=atom
    card=many
    ask="which worlds?"
    doc="With reasoner=matrix: makes this world a composite (spec 15, composite worlds): its library instance is built from the legends, knowledge bases and matrices of the named worlds plus its own matrix. The named worlds keep their own isolated instances; nothing is composed implicitly."

@core.world.reads core.key
    value=atom
    card=many
    ask="which worlds?"
    doc="With reasoner=matrix: worlds whose legends and knowledge bases this world's matrix reads facts of (kids.arith reads the purchases of kids.shop). Their wires are copied into this world's library instance; their matrices are not loaded and nothing else is shared (spec 15, one instance per world)."

@core.world.undo core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="which action?"
    doc="With reasoner=matrix: the action that takes the last move back (for example ttt.undo). The host layer answers it by rewinding the library to before the last turn that changed it, and the world's fns.mjs `undoWords` says what was taken back. Worlds that do not set it keep their own undo operation."

@core.world.redo core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="which action?"
    doc="With reasoner=matrix and undo=: the action that puts back what the last undo took out (for example doc.redo). The host layer re-applies it from the marks the undo kept; a turn that changes the library empties them."

@core.world.passive core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="true or false?"
    doc="With reasoner=matrix: true for a world whose state follows the other worlds (the shell's tab: an editor brings its tab forward). What another world's request changed in it is not a step of the turn, so undoing that turn leaves it alone; only a turn of the world's own undoes its changes."

@core.world.untold core.key
    value=atom
    card=many
    ask="which wire types?"
    doc="With reasoner=matrix: wire types the world's operations emit (for example the sentences of a document) that only the session memory keeps; the library does not hold them. For facts the engine reads from its own state, where telling them to the library would cost more than it gives."

@core.world.reasoner core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="ops or matrix?"
    doc="ops (default): the world answers through operations.sop and ops.mjs. matrix: it also ships matrix.sop (and fns.mjs) and answers through the sopworld library when the engine runs with the matrix reasoner (spec 15)."

files.mapping.sop:
# How PSys2 legends map onto the library's schema (worker-tasks G2, G8.1).
# Tell this before the legends; the legends are then loaded unchanged.

# A key declaration: the id is <type>.<key>; value= holds literal kinds and $type references.
@psys2.map.key core.schema.map from=core.key
    owner=id.prefix key=id.suffix
    value=value many=card:many required=required ask=ask default=default
    prefix=dynamic          # dynamic=true: any key <key>.<anything> (where.owner, arg.count)

# A type declaration: the id is the type name; a type that names no parent extends core.thing.
@psys2.map.type core.schema.map from=core.type as=type
    name=id extends=extends closed=closed root=core.thing
    complete=closed        # in PSys2 closed=true also means: the world knows every instance
    shared=shared          # the library's shared=true (the facts of the type belong to every namespace): the host adds it to the legend text of the agents (src/reasoner/ns.mjs)

# A legend is a module: namespace= names it, imports= names what it needs.
@psys2.map.legend core.schema.map from=core.legend as=module
    name=namespace imports=imports
